solution:
Subtracting 5, we get

\(-7 - 5 < 2x \le 9 - 5\)

\(-12 < 2x \le 4\)

Dividing by 2, we get

\(-6 < x \le 2\)

So, \(x \in (-6, 2]\).

context: Solve the following inequalities and write the solution set using interval notation.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the printed solution reaches the correct inequality \(\frac{x-4}{x-3} \le 0\) and its own sign table marks the middle region, but then states the solution set as \((-\infty, 3) \cup [4, \infty)\) — the region where that expression is \(\ge 0\). The correct answer is \((3, 4]\): at \(x = 3.5\) the original left side is \(7 \ge 4\) (so 3.5 belongs, yet the printed set excludes it), while at \(x = 5\) it is \(2.5 < 4\) (so 5 does not belong, yet the printed set includes it).]

subtracting, 4, we get

[Note that, as we do not know value of \(x\), we do not multiply by \((x - 3)\)]

\(\frac{x}{x-3} - 4 \ge 0\)

\(\frac{x - 4(x-3)}{x-3} \ge 0\)

\(\frac{x - 4x + 12}{x-3} \ge 0\)

\(\frac{-3x + 12}{x-3} \ge 0\)

\(\frac{-3(x-4)}{x-3} \ge 0\)

Dividing by \(-3\), we get

Say \(p(x) = \frac{x-4}{x-3} \le 0\)

Take \(x = 3, 4\) as critical points. It divides number line into 3 regions as follows.

| Regions | \((x \le 3)\) | \((3 \le x \le 4)\) | \((x \ge 4)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test Points | \(2\) | \(3.5\) | \(5\) |
| Sign of \(x - 4\) | \(-\)ve | \(-\)ve | \(+\)ve |
| Sign of \(x - 3\) | \(-\)ve | \(+\)ve | \(+\)ve |
| Sign of \(p(x)\) | \(p(x) > 0\) Except at \(x = 3\) | \(p(x) < 0\) | \(p(x) > 0\) |

The solution set is \((x < 3)\) and \((x \ge 4)\). So \(x \in (-\infty, 3) \cup [4, \infty)\).

Here \(x = 3\) is not in the solution set, as it makes denominator 0.
_note: Printed defect, transcribed as printed (NOT repaired). The book's own derivation ends at p(x) = (x-4)/(x-3) <= 0 and its own sign table marks p(x) < 0 only in the middle region, so the solution set should be (3, 4]; the printed conclusion (-inf, 3) U [4, inf) is the region where p(x) >= 0, i.e. the opposite. Numerical check on the ORIGINAL inequality x/(x-3) >= 4: x = 3.5 gives 7 (satisfies, but is excluded by the printed answer) and x = 5 gives 2.5 (fails, but is included by the printed answer). Secondary defect: the printed region headers use <= / >= so the three regions overlap at the critical points x = 3 and x = 4, and x = 3 is not admissible at all.
